text:
lina: Ran a bunch of attention sweeps this morning: SplitFlash (our hybrid split-kernel) vs FlashPaged vs fused-paged on A100 / H100 / L40s. Seeing a weird throughput dip on H100 when batch >= 32. Uploading traces.
perf-bot: benchmark started: run_id=run-2026-03-18-09-24, configs: seq=[32,64,128,256,512], batch=[1,4,8,16,32,64], gpus=[A100,H100,L40s]. artifacts: /bench/run-2026-03-18-09-24/
sam: :eyes: can you paste the offending numbers?
lina: quick snippet from aggregated CSV (tokens/s):
```
gpu,model,batch,seq,tokens_per_sec
H100,SplitFlash,16,256,1.2M
H100,SplitFlash,32,256,760k  <-- drop
H100,FlashPaged,32,256,1.05M
A100,SplitFlash,32,256,1.15M
L40s,SplitFlash,32,256,680k
```
vikram: interesting — only SplitFlash on H100 drops, FlashPaged unaffected. Could be a kernel-fallback or memory path thrash. Any KV-cache spikes?
lina: checked kv-evict metrics. There's a small bump in evictions at batch 32 on H100 (per-shard evict_count +25%) and a higher memcpy time in the perf trace.
maria: can you share the perf flamegraph? link?
lina: https://artifacts.internal/bench/run-2026-03-18-09-24/flame-h100-splitflash-b32-seq256.svg
noah: looked at the flamegraph — the big delta is in cuMemcpyAsync and a kernel called "split_attention_tail" that suddenly runs more often. Might be kv cache page alignment forcing extra copies.
vikram: that matches my theory. If SplitFlash uses a different block tiling it may hit a different allocator path on H100 at certain batch*seq shapes. Could also be workspace allocator fragmentation.
sam: any config change recently to kernel selector thresholds? I remember we lowered the "seq-to-kvratio" cutoff last week.
lina: yes — PR #4321 adjusted selector: prefer_split_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.55 to prefer SplitFlash at more shapes. The change rolled to staged yesterday.
maria: maybe SplitFlash is being picked in cases where FlashPaged would have been faster on H100. Can we force the selector to fallback for batch>=32 and rerun quickly?
lina: patching a quick override in runtime to bias selector: if gpu==H100 && batch>=32 -> prefer FlashPaged. Running single-shot now.
perf-bot: quick run finished: run-2026-03-18-09-34-override. Artifacts: /bench/run-2026-03-18-09-34-override/
lina: override results: H100, SplitFlash forced->FlashPaged at batch32 seq256 = 1.04M tokens/s (restored). So selector bias was likely the root cause.
noah: ok that suggests revert or tighten threshold only for H100. But still want to understand why SplitFlash regresses on H100 specifically. Could be driver shim or cuBLAS path.
vikram: next: capture kernel launch params (block sizes, shared mem) for the failing runs and compare. I'll add extra tracepoints to the kernel harness.
sam: I'll run the batch/seq grid on L40s to ensure no cross-regression.
lina: created a small reproducer: `./run_perf --gpu H100 --model splitflash --batch 32 --seq 256 --iters 200 --trace kernel_launch.csv`
maria: also add `--workspace-stats` and `--kv-alloc-log` to the run. Those logs will show spills.
lina: good call. putting a bisect on prefer_split_threshold between 0.55..0.7 and will run on H100 fleet tomorrow morning.
noah: if bisect is clear, we should ship a quick runtime hotfix: per-gpu selector table instead of global threshold.
sam: :+1: I'll own the L40s checks and smaller batches.
perf-bot: artifacts uploaded for all runs. Summary: regression caused by selector bias; mitigation: per-gpu override; follow-ups: kernel launch tracing, allocator stats, bisect PR. Links: /bench/run-2026-03-18-09-24/, /bench/run-2026-03-18-09-34-override/ :rocket:
lina: thanks team. Opening issue #INF-721 with logs + reproducer. Will update with bisect results. :thinking_face:
